commit.message:
Convert XLS cell values when importing a Databook

XLSFormat.import_book re-implemented the row loop with raw sheet.row_values(),
so the same file loaded as a Databook returned Excel date serials and raw error
codes where a Dataset returned datetime objects and strings like #N/A.

Extract an import_sheet classmethod, mirroring the XLSX and ODS formats, and
call it from both import_set and import_book so the two paths cannot drift
again. The cell conversion moves into a read_cell classmethod, matching the ODS
format, with the workbook datemode passed in explicitly.

Fix TypeError when stacking two headerless Datasets with stack_cols

Dataset.stack_cols() explicitly permits two headerless datasets: the
header guard only raises HeadersNeeded when exactly one side has headers,
and the header concatenation catches None + None to set new_headers=None.
But it then did 'for column in self.headers', which iterates None and
raised 'TypeError: NoneType object is not iterable', so column-level
stacking crashed on inputs that row-level stack() handles fine.

When neither dataset has headers, iterate columns by index with get_col()
instead of by header name. The headered path is unchanged.

Fix ODS export of boolean values crashing on re-import

In Python bool is a subclass of int, so a True/False cell matched the
numbers. Number branch in ODSFormat.dset_sheet and was written with
valuetype="float" and value=True. odfpy serializes that as the string
"True", and on import read_cell runs float("True") for a float cell,
raising ValueError. read_cell already has a boolean value-type reader
that the export side never exercised.

Emit booleans with valuetype="boolean" and the matching booleanvalue so
they round-trip back as Python bool.

Fix ODS export of boolean values crashing on re-import

In Python bool is a subclass of int, so a True/False cell matched the
numbers. Number branch in ODSFormat.dset_sheet and was written with
valuetype="float" and value=True. odfpy serializes that as the string
"True", and on import read_cell runs float("True") for a float cell,
raising ValueError. read_cell already has a boolean value-type reader
that the export side never exercised.

Emit booleans with valuetype="boolean" and the matching booleanvalue so
they round-trip back as Python bool.

commit.message:
Only strip the leading '=' when escaping XLSX formulae

When escape=True, formula cells had every '=' removed via
cell.value.replace('=', ''), but the option is documented to strip only
the leading '='. A comparison formula like =A1=B1 was corrupted to A1B1
instead of A1=B1. Removing just the leading '=' already disables the
formula, so stripping inner '=' is unnecessary data loss.

Replace the replace('=', '') with cell.value[1:] (the leading '=' is
guaranteed by the startswith('=') guard) and add a regression test.

Raise TypeError for invalid Dataset instance

stack() and stack_cols() currently return None silently when passed a non-Dataset argument. This can hide bugs since callers get None back and may not notice the operation failed.

This commit raises TypeError with a clear message instead.

commit.message:
Preserve column order in YAML export

yaml.safe_dump sorts mapping keys alphabetically by default, so YAML export
reordered columns (e.g. apple, id, name, zebra) inconsistently with the CSV and
JSON exports, which keep the dataset's header order.

Pass sort_keys=False when dumping the dataset and databook so YAML keeps the
original column order.

Fixes #287
